newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers bet on comfortable supplies.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers bet on comfortable supplies.

text.p: Germany's chocolate industry believes cocoa futures rallies are exaggerated and belie good underlying supplies, traders said on Thursday.
"Consumers expect a normal Ivorian 97/98 crop and recent rallies have brought out a lot of cocoa from other origins so they feel no need to buy in the physical market," one said.
"They also think it is too early to fear supply problems in Latin America, Asia and West Africa from El Nino (dry weather patterns)."
Traders said consumers had taken some early 97/98 supplies of beans and butter when futures rallied to eight-year highs last week.
But the combination of high prices and an unfavourable sterling/mark ratio had now over-ridden supply fears.
"I get the impression there are ample stocks around, both at trade and industry level," another trader said.
Traders also attributed the futures rallies as spill-over from the overheated coffee market and to one European manufacturer's building of a long position.
Third quarter cif bean prices for good West African quality were put at 3.08 marks/kg, having risen some 0.25 marks from end-May levels.
Fourth quarter beans were at 3.07 and first quarter 1998 beans at 3.01.
Spot cocoa butter cost 7.30 marks per kg liquid ex-works on the basis of a 2.36 ratio.

This represented a 0.35 marks rise in June although the ratio has fallen by seven points. Third quarter butter was at 7.50 marks (2.39 ratio) and fourth quarter at 7.58 marks (2.45). -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
